I have farmed this small piece of land since I was a girl, and it feeds me when the rains are good. I do not buy chemical fertilizer because one bag costs more money than I have, and my arms are too old to carry such a heavy thing from the shop to my plot. I will put cow dung and compost from behind my house on the soil, plant the seed I kept from last season with my own hands, and my daughter will come to help me weed and harvest when the time comes. We can finish all the work ourselves in about ten days over the season; I have no money to pay hired workers.
